comparison.cold: DreamCoder L0 is the first iteration-0 174-task generative enumeration call and first 30-goal test run. F-system cold acquisition starts each train Goal from a fresh L0.
comparison.learned: DreamCoder uses two official wake-sleep/compression iterations. F-system accumulates the same seed curriculum into a persistent Library before paired unseen search.

runtime_compatibility_notes: Windows has no SIGVTALRM/SIGPROF. Task.check and Helmholtz runWithTimeout install narrowly scoped Python profile hooks that raise the corresponding official timeout exception at Python call/return boundaries after the thread-CPU deadline. C-extension calls cannot be pre-empted until control returns to Python.

OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS/NumExpr/VECLIB/BLIS and PyTorch intra-op/inter-op threads are explicitly capped at one in both systems. Three incomplete seed-17 attempts are archived under aborted_attempts and excluded: the first used PyTorch's environment-default 12-thread pool; the second used one thread but stalled under the original soft task timeout; the third reached Helmholtz sampling but exhausted available memory under the original post-call generated-program timeout.
The pinned source _unfold contains a free-variable typo (f); runtime bridge binds the intended emit argument h. F uses the same repaired semantics.
PyPy is not installed in the supplied environment. The official PyPy compressor algorithm is invoked in-process under CPython; process/interpreter isolation is absent.
Official source tree is not modified; all compatibility and typo handling is in this experiment adapter.

Optional parameterized pickle checkpoint/graph export is disabled because the full Windows path exceeds MAX_PATH; the official search/learning loop still runs and raw JSON captures its frontiers, grammars, timing, and evaluation counters.

execution.affinity_failure_policy: If Windows refuses affinity, retain one-thread/CPUs=1 limits and record affinity_set=false; no scheduler redesign or budget change.
execution.on_seed_failure: Preserve partial raw/log/status, stop that seed, continue other seeds; no retry or budget extension.

f_system.accumulation: One curriculum stream per seed with normal persistent Library formation and usage; then save, cold reload, and verify hash/sidecar.
f_system.cold_acquisition: Each training Goal starts independently from a fresh L0; new F must use normal formation and required admission before commit.
f_system.library_initial_state: 22 DreamCoder-mapped semantic leaves plus 11 generic syntax slots; no preloaded composite F.
f_system.paired_unseen_conditions: Each unseen Goal/condition cold-loads the same accumulated Library and usage sidecar; FIRST_CLASS exposes admitted composites, EXPANDED masks their direct candidate/retrieval path while leaving ancestors and primitives available. Both may learn in-memory; each task run is isolated, and test-time mutations are not written to the accumulated checkpoint.

failure_policy: No protocol change, timeout increase, task or primitive substitution, or retries after a seed result. Only a confirmed common code bug permits a new revision and restart of all three seeds.

hard_wall_clock_guard.after_limit: terminate only the exceeded seed process tree, annotate partial raw and status, continue the other seeds
hard_wall_clock_guard.applies_to: each concurrent DreamCoder seed process tree, including startup and writing outputs

metrics.unavailable_metric_policy: N/A; do not modify official DreamCoder kernel to manufacture counters.
metrics.units_note: DreamCoder program checks and F-system candidate probes are separately named; native search budgets are not asserted to be equivalent.

objective: Compare library formation and reuse under the same fixed small compute budget without attempting DreamCoder's published peak performance.
project: Resource-bounded DreamCoder List Processing and F-system V9.4 comparison
reporting_statement: Resource-bounded reproduction using the official DreamCoder List Processing implementation and DSL, under a fixed reduced compute budget. FAST results are not intended to reproduce DreamCoder's published peak performance; they compare library formation and reuse behavior under a tractable fixed compute budget.
revision_reason: Revision 1 varied DreamCoder --random-seed across runs, which also changed randomized task generation and the split. Revision 2 fixed that split but torch.manual_seed() invoked all-device seeding and all three processes faulted in the NVIDIA driver; F-system serialization also called a nonexistent domain method. Revision 3 switched to CPU-only PyTorch seeding and the existing module-level AST serializer, but the first F-system seed then failed at Library persistence because its output directory did not exist. Revision 4 creates the per-seed output directory before saving. All three F-system seeds restart; DreamCoder remains excluded after the repeated host-level NVIDIA driver failure and is not retried.
